pr_title: tree: fix serialization of null values in tuples with enums
pr_body:
Enum values need to be serialized in a special way - with the type
annotation containing an Oid type reference. Previously, NULL values
when used in a tuple with enum values had a different type annotation
which caused the remote nodes to hit an assertion about not being able
to resolve the type by name.

Fixes: #58889.

Release note (bug fix): Previously, CockroachDB could encounter an
internal error when executing queries with tuples containing null values
and enums in a distributed setting, and this is now fixed.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/58894)

I'm not very familiar with this code, and the fix was inspired by https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/d00f2c75c69e771e66e96192903071181e695667/pkg/sql/sem/tree/format.go#L389-L398 which was most recently touched by Rafi, hence I added you as the reviewer. I'm also happy to hand the issue to SQL Experience for a proper fix (if this isn't) :)

issue_context.title: sql: problem with type checking enums on the remote nodes
issue_context.body:
Extracted from [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/58285#issuecomment-755132738).

Reproduction steps (on a 3 node demo cluster):
```
CREATE TYPE greeting AS ENUM ('hello', 'howdy', 'hi', 'good day', 'morning');
CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT enum_range('hello'::greeting)[g] as _enum FROM generate_series(1, 5) as g;
ALTER TABLE t SPLIT AT SELECT i FROM generate_series(1, 5) as g(i);
ALTER TABLE t SCATTER;
SELECT _enum FROM t WHERE _enum::greeting IN (NULL, 'hi':::greeting);
```
Results in
```
ERROR: internal error: unable to vectorize execution plan: "$0" IN (NULL::public.greeting, b'\x80':::@100052): unsupported comparison operator: "$0" IN (NULL::public.greeting, b'\x80':::@100052): cannot resolve types in DistSQL by name
SQLSTATE: XX000
DETAIL: stack trace:
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/execinfrapb/expr.go:81: processExpression()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/execinfrapb/expr.go:154: DeserializeExpr()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/execinfrapb/expr.go:183: Init()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/rowexec/filterer.go:61: newFiltererProcessor()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/rowexec/processors.go:144: NewProcessor()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/colbuilder/execplan.go:573: func1()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/colbuilder/execplan.go:95: wrapRowSources()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/colbuilder/execplan.go:561: createAndWrapRowSource()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/colbuilder/execplan.go:1302: planAndMaybeWrapFilter()
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/colexec/colbuilder/execplan.go:762: NewColOperator()
...
```
It looks like we somehow fail to deserialize `'hi':::greeting` part of the filter on the remote node.

The problem is present when using the row-by-row engine too.

cc @arulajmani in case you're curious to take a look
